title: MSP-MVS: Multi-granularity Segmentation Prior Guided Multi-View Stereo

predicted_errors.error_location: SECTION::2 (Proposed Method) vs Abstract, Conclusion, and Method Details
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: SECTION::2 states: 'Therefore, we propose TSAR-MVS, a generalized post-processing MVS method that sequentially applies confidence-based outliers filtering, superpixel-based local refinement, and feature-based area generation to planarize textureless areas.' This describes TSAR-MVS — a real, separately published paper by Yuan et al. (2024b) in Pattern Recognition (Vol. 154, Article 110565). TSAR-MVS is correctly acknowledged as PRIOR WORK in SECTION::3 (Related Work): 'TAPA-MVS..., PCF-MVS... and TSAR-MVS (Yuan et al. 2024b) attempt to employ superpixel planarization.' Yet SECTION::2 presents TSAR-MVS as the authors' own proposed method. Meanwhile, the Abstract, SECTION::4 (Method Details), SECTION::5 (Experiments), and SECTION::6 (Conclusion) all describe a completely different method: MSP-MVS (using Semantic-SAM for multi-granularity depth edges, anchor equidistribution, and ILS optimization). The contributions listed in SECTION::2 — joint hypothesis filter, iterative correlation refinement with RANSAC+WMF, textureless-aware segmentation with Roberts edge detection and Hough line detection — are TSAR-MVS's contributions, not MSP-MVS's. The ablation studies in SECTION::5 test MSP-MVS components (multi-granularity segmentation prior, anchor equidistribution, ILS), none of which are introduced in the contributions list. This constitutes a fundamental identity confusion: the paper cannot simultaneously be about TSAR-MVS (as claimed in the Proposed Method section) and MSP-MVS (as claimed everywhere else). Web verification confirms TSAR-MVS is a real, previously published paper by different primary authors.

predicted_errors.error_location: SECTION::2 (Contributions list) vs SECTION::4, SECTION::5 (Method Details and Experiments)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The contributions explicitly claimed in SECTION::2 are: (1) joint hypothesis filter, (2) iterative correlation refinement with RANSAC+WMF, (3) textureless-aware segmentation with edge/line detection, (4) SOTA results. However, the method actually described and evaluated in SECTIONS 4-6 is MSP-MVS with entirely different components: (1) multi-granularity segmentation prior via Semantic-SAM, (2) anchor equidistribution with 8-sector division, (3) iterative local search (ILS) optimization. The ablation studies in SECTION::5 test MSP-MVS components (w/o. SAM, w/o. Her, w/o. Agr., w/o. CRF., w/o. Avg., w/o. Cls., w/o. Equ., w/o. Var., w/o. Cst., w/o. ILS), none of which correspond to any claimed contribution. The contributions list therefore does not describe the paper being evaluated.

SECTION::4 contains near-duplicate text spanning two paragraphs that describe the same concept in nearly identical language. Paragraph 1 (line 39): 'Due to the absence of depth edge as constraints, APD-MVS erroneously skips depth edges to select anchor within heterogeneous areas, thereby causing potential inaccuracy. While by introducing semantic awareness and granularity richness, Semantic-SAM can achieve panoramic segmentation at any granularity level, which contains potential depth edges. Therefore, we adopt the Semantic-SAM to extract multi-granularity depth edges for patch deformation.' Paragraph 2 (lines 41-42): 'Since APD-MVS lacks depth edge guidance, its anchors typically skip depth edges to be selected within green heterogeneous areas, causing potential inaccuracy. Therefore, we attempt to extract depth edges as guidance for patch deformation.... Differently, by introducing semantic awareness and granularity richness, Semantic-SAM can achieve panoramic segmentation at any granularity level, which may contain potential depth edges. Therefore, we attempt to adopt Semantic-SAM to extract multi-granularity depth edges for patch deformation.' These two paragraphs make the same argument using near-identical phrasing, suggesting incomplete editing or text generation artifacts. This is material because it indicates the methodology description was not properly finalized.

The paper is titled and branded as MSP-MVS throughout the Abstract ('we introduce Multi-granularity Segmentation Prior Multi-View Stereo (MSP-MVS)') and Conclusion ('we introduce MSP-MVS, a novel MVS method'). However, SECTION::2 introduces the method as: 'Therefore, we propose TSAR-MVS, a generalized post-processing MVS method.' TSAR-MVS is a real, separate publication by Yuan et al. (2024b) in Pattern Recognition. This is not a simple naming error — the entire method description in SECTION::2 (joint hypothesis filter, iterative correlation refinement with RANSAC+WMF, textureless-aware segmentation with Roberts edge and Hough line detection) describes TSAR-MVS's technical approach, which is fundamentally different from MSP-MVS's approach (Semantic-SAM depth edges, anchor equidistribution, ILS optimization). The paper has an identity crisis: it cannot be both TSAR-MVS and MSP-MVS.

summary: CRITICAL FINDING: The paper suffers from a fundamental identity confusion. The abstract, title, method details, experiments, and conclusion all describe MSP-MVS — a method using Semantic-SAM for multi-granularity depth edge extraction, anchor equidistribution, and iterative local search optimization. However, the Proposed Method section (SECTION::2) describes TSAR-MVS — a completely different method (joint hypothesis filter, iterative correlation refinement with RANSAC+WMF, textureless-aware segmentation with Roberts edge and Hough line detection). Web verification confirms TSAR-MVS is a real, separately published paper by Yuan et al. (2024b) in Pattern Recognition, which the paper's own Related Work section correctly cites as prior work. The contributions list in SECTION::2 enumerates TSAR-MVS's contributions, not MSP-MVS's. Additionally, SECTION::4 contains near-duplicate paragraphs (lines 39-42) that make the same argument twice with nearly identical wording, indicating incomplete editing. The ablation studies in SECTION::5 correctly correspond to MSP-MVS components, suggesting the experimental results are for MSP-MVS, but the paper's core methodological claim is contaminated by improperly adapted text from the TSAR-MVS paper. This paper requires major revision to resolve the identity conflict, properly attribute TSAR-MVS as prior work, align the contributions list with MSP-MVS's actual components, and remove duplicated text.
